metadata.title: Riyadh Connected Desert Systems & Dust Transport Corridors
metadata.description: Spatial geometries, distances, and corridor vectors of the 5 key desert systems directly affecting sandstorms in Riyadh

properties.name: Al-Thumamah Desert Dunes
properties.sand_type: Active longitudinal dunes, fine quartz sand sheets
properties.emission_mechanism: High sensitivity to local wind gusts (>= 7 m/s) and diurnal thermal turbulence, producing fast local blowing dust and rapid visibility drops in northern and eastern Riyadh.

properties.name: Ad-Dahna Desert (Eastern Sand Sea)
properties.sand_type: Iron-oxide coated reddish dunes (barchans and star dunes)
properties.emission_mechanism: Acts as the physical eastern sand bridge linking northern Nafud to southern Rub' al-Khali; funnels high concentrations of red silt/sand directly into central Riyadh under easterly or migrating Shamal wind vectors.

properties.name: Nafud al-Thuwairat (Northern Sand Sea)
properties.sand_type: Fine aeolian silts, unconsolidated dune sands
properties.emission_mechanism: Classified by the Saudi Regional SDS Center as one of the most active sand-emission hotspots; dominant northwesterly Shamal winds mobilize fine particulate matter that travels down the Al-Qassim/Al-Majmaah corridor straight into Riyadh.

properties.name: Tuwayq Escarpment
properties.sand_type: Limestone plateau, talus slopes, desert wadi alluvial deposits
properties.emission_mechanism: 800-km continuous cliff cuesta creating severe topographic wind channeling, thermal updrafts, and convective downdraft Haboobs that sweep dust walls into Riyadh.

properties.name: Rub' al-Khali (The Empty Quarter)
properties.sand_type: Massive transverse dunes, mega-barchans, hypersaline sabkhas
properties.emission_mechanism: World's largest sand sea; deep southerly thermal depressions and Khasif wind surges drive massive, regional dust plumes northward across southern Riyadh Province into the capital.
